text: The stack in four sentences An NNX module is a Python object whose arrays live in typed Variables ; every JAX transformation sees it as two things, a static, hashable graphdef (the structure, which keys the compile cache) and a state (a pytree of arrays).

text: An optax optimiser is a pair of pure functions over pytrees, built by chaining small transformations, so its state is just more arrays.
label: core

text: An orbax checkpoint is any pytree written shard by shard, asynchronously, restorable into whatever shapes and shardings you hand it.
label: core

text: A grain pipeline computes every record from its index and a seed, so the loader's whole position is a few integers that go into the same checkpoint.

section: 7. float16 and loss scaling
text: Measured on one batch at the initial weights, gradients computed through a float16 copy of the model measured : At S = 1 few gradients become exactly zero, but many land among float16's subnormals and lose precision: the median relative error is about ten times that at S = 256. bfloat16 at S = 1 has a larger median error still (8 significant bits against float16's 11) but loses nothing to range; its handful of zeros are sums that cancel, not underflow.

section: 7. float16 and loss scaling
text: Dynamic loss scaling searches for the largest safe S: start high, halve S and skip the step whenever a gradient is not finite, double it after a run of good steps. jmp's DynamicLossScale (the reference implementation, last released 2023) does this as a small pytree you carry through the jitted step; PyTorch's torch.amp.GradScaler is the same algorithm. ls = jmp.DynamicLossScale(jnp.asarray(2.0 ** 15, jnp.float32)) @jax.jit def step(p, s, ls, x, y): def f(pc): logits = MJ.apply(jax.tree.map(lambda a: a.astype(jnp.float16), pc), x, CFG).astype(jnp.float32) return ls.scale(optax.softmax_cross_entropy_with_integer_labels(logits, y).mean()) l, g = jax.value_and_grad(f)(p) # float32 master weights; float16 inside g = ls.unscale(g) finite = jmp.all_finite(g) u, s2 = tx.update(g, s, p) p, s = jmp.select_tree(finite, (optax.apply_updates(p, u), s2), (p, s)) # skip the step on overflow return p, s, ls.adjust(finite), ls.unscale(l), finite 200 steps, float16 compute with float32 master weights Difference of each run's training loss from the float32 run, every 10 steps, and validation loss after 200 steps on the Training lab's 8 validation batches ( src/runs/ts_mixed.py ) measured .

section: 8. evaluation loops and metrics
text: Evaluation loops and metrics The problem. loss.item() every step is harmless in eager PyTorch on CPU but on an accelerator it forces the host to wait for the device, serialising a pipeline that JAX runs asynchronously (dispatch returns before the device finishes).

section: 8. evaluation loops and metrics
text: The fix is to accumulate metrics on the device, inside the compiled step, and read them every N steps. nnx.MultiMetric(loss=nnx.metrics.Average("loss"), accuracy=nnx.metrics.Accuracy()) is a module whose state is running sums in Variables; metrics.update(loss=..., logits=..., labels=...) inside an nnx.jit step adds to them on device; metrics.compute() and reset() on the host every N steps are the only syncs (source ; also Welford for mean and variance).
